scenes.text: This is the plan for a shared visual explainer. One skill renders one fixed HTML page from a props file, for every plan, milestone gate and pull request review.

The goal: one shared skill renders every explainer from a props JSON file, so each run looks the same. I need you to approve two things: a fixed HTML page instead of a per-run Remotion video, and a path and line reference on each hand-test step. The top risks: a failed explainer could block a milestone, and a wrong code reference could look like proof.

We are done when the render script writes one self-contained page in both modes, invalid props fail with one field-path error each, props text cannot inject markup, the three callers run the right mode, and a failed explainer never blocks a park or a resume.
Four phases in one lane. First the renderer, the schemas and the template, test-first. Then the skill text and the example props. Then the three callers. A review phase closes the milestone.

Before, each run built its own Remotion project. After, the three callers use one shared renderer. The skill text, the schemas, the render script and the page template are new. The check mode prints one field-path error for each line.

Three decisions. Animate with SVG and CSS inside the page, not with a Remotion video or an MP4 render. The agent writes only props JSON, never HTML. And each ship hand-test step must carry a path and line reference.
Out of scope: no video in this milestone, no themes for each caller, and no npm dependencies in the renderer. And do not chase pixel parity with the old Remotion scenes.
That is the plan: four phases and three decisions, ready for review. Open the report page for the full detail.
